Tosafot on Bava Batra 144a:1:1.hebrew: אודייני - פי' בקונטרס: בור וכסויו. ואין נראה לרבינו תם, אלא מפרש שהוא כלי גבוה שעומדים עליו שומרי שדות וכרמים, לראות מעליו למרחוק, וגם הוא ראוי לישן עליו, כדאמרינן בפרק בתרא דמועד קטן (דף כז.): ישן על גבי מטה, או על גבי ספסל, או על גבי אודייני. ויש ספרים שכתוב בהן "אידווני", כמו "דוי" להכא ולהכא (תמיד דף כו: ובשבת לה.):
Tosafot on Bava Batra 144a:1:1.english: Udyanei - Rashi explains in the Kuntres: a pit and its cover. But this does not seem right to Rabbeinu Tam, who instead explains that it is a tall structure on which the guards of fields and vineyards stand, to look out from above into the distance, and it is also suitable for sleeping on, as we say in the last chapter of Moed Katan (27a): "[If a mourner] slept on a bed, or on a bench, or on an udyanei." And there are books in which it is written "idvanei," like "davui" [meaning to lean] to one side and the other (Tamid 26b and Shabbat 35a):

Tosafot on Bava Batra 144a:3:1.hebrew: באשה יורשת - פירש בקונטרס: כגון ראובן שנשא בת שמעון אחיו, ומת יעקב אביהם, ואחר כך מתו ראובן ושמעון — שאז יורשין בני ראובן ובת שמעון מאביהן. וקצת קשה לישנא דראו מה שהניח לי בעלי, דמשמע דירשה מבעלה ולא מיעקב. ופירש ריב"ם: אשה יורשת — שנשא ראובן בת שמעון אחיו ומת, והיו לו לראובן אחים קטנים או בני אחים קטנים דהוו יתמי, והרי היא יורשת את בעלה עם הקטנים, שהיא במקום אביה. ומיהו קשה, דקאמרי' בסמוך דטרחא קמי יתמי, דמשמע בני בעלה. על כן נראה לר"י כפירוש הקונטרס, דכיון שבעל אוכל פירות ירושתה כל ימי חייו כדין, שייך שפיר "ראו מה שהניח לי בעלי". אי נמי כלשון אחר שפירש בקונטרס, שאמר הבעל: תטול האשה כאחד מן הבנים:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 144a:3:1.english: A woman who inherits - Rashi explained: For example, Reuven married the daughter of his brother Shimon, and their father Yaakov died, and afterward Reuven and Shimon died — so that Reuven's sons and Shimon's daughter inherit from their grandfather. This is somewhat difficult, though, given the wording "See what my husband left me," which implies that she inherited from her husband and not from Yaakov. And Rivam explained: [The case of] a woman who inherits is where Reuven married the daughter of his brother Shimon and died, and Reuven had minor brothers or sons of minor brothers who were orphans, and she inherits her husband together with the minors, since she stands in the place of her father. But this is difficult, because [the Gemara] says shortly afterward that she labored before the orphans, which implies the sons of her husband. Therefore it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that [one should follow] the explanation of Rashi: since a husband legitimately enjoys the produce of her inheritance all the days of his life, it is quite fitting to say "See what my husband left me." Alternatively, [it can be understood] like the other explanation that Rashi gave, that the husband said: Let the wife take a share like one of the sons:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 144a:5:1.hebrew: ואם אמרה ראו מה שהניח לי בעלי - פירש בקונטרס: וכיון דאמרה הכי, לית לה מזוני. ואין נראה לרשב"א דדוקא אם מכרה כתובתה, או לקחה כתובתה בבית דין, אין לה מזונות; אבל זו שלא לקחה כלום מכתובתה, אלא נכסי מלוג שלה, או מה שירשה, או מה שנתן לה בעלה כאחד מן הבנים — לא הפסידה מזונות. דאפי' מכרה מקצת כתובתה, אמרינן בפרק אלמנה (כתובות דף צח.) דלית דחש ליה לדר' שמעון דאמר מקצת כסף ככל כסף, ולא הפסידה מזונות; כ"ש נכסי מלוג, דלא שייכי כלל לכתובתה. וגם מה שפירש שאם נתעצלו בית דין להשביעה, מה שהשביחה לעצמה — לא ידע רשב"א מנליה; דלעולם הויא בחזקת יורשים עד שישביעוה ב"ד, דאין לה כח לגבות כתובתה אלא בבית דין. והכא מיירי דוקא באשה יורשת:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 144a:5:1.english: "And if she said: 'See what my husband left me'" - Rashi explained in the Kuntres: Since she said this, she has no maintenance. But this does not seem right to the Rashba, [namely] that only if she sold her ketubah, or collected her ketubah in court, does she have no maintenance. But one who did not take anything from her ketubah, but [only] her nikhsei melog (usufruct property), or what she inherited, or what her husband gave her as [he would] to one of the sons — she has not lost her maintenance. For even if she sold part of her ketubah, we say in the chapter Almanah (Ketubot 98a) that no one is concerned about the view of R. Shimon, who says that "part of the money is like all of the money," and she did not lose her maintenance; all the more so [in the case of] nikhsei melog, which have no connection at all to her ketubah. And also, regarding what [Rashi] explained, that if the court was negligent in making her swear, what she improved is for herself — the Rashba did not know from where he derived this; for [the property] always remains in the presumptive possession of the heirs until the court makes her swear, since she has no power to collect her ketubah except through the court. And here [the Gemara] speaks only of a woman who is an heir.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 144a:7:1.hebrew: בית ואכסדרה מהו - דנהי דעלייה לא קנה, אכסדרה שייכא טפי לגבי בית. ואם תמצא לומר לא קנה משום דאין בו תשמיש בית — שני בתים זה לפנים מזה מהו? דכבית אחד דמי? ולפירוש הקונטרס הוה ליה להקדים בעיא דשני בתים לבית ואכסדרה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 144a:7:1.english: "A house and a portico — what is the law?" - For although he did not acquire the upper story, a portico is more closely connected to a house. And if you say that he did not acquire [the upper story] because it has no use as a house — what is the law of two houses, one inside the other? Are they considered like one house? And according to the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], [the Gemara] should have put the question about two houses before the question about a house and a portico:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 144a:9:1.english: Like a halakhah without a reason - There is some reason. Since [the son] vacated the house, the son's mind is set at ease, and also he has nowhere else to live, so it is reasonable that [the father] gave it to him. Likewise, one who writes all his property to his wife or to his son presumably did not intend to give it to her outright, but only to honor her, since he would not leave his sons with nothing at all. And in a transfer in the presence of all three, the Sages did not want to trouble [the parties] to bring witnesses and perform a kinyan, because presumably, since he said it to him in the presence of the three of them, he transferred it to him completely. And it appears to Rabbi Yitzchak (the Ri) that in a transfer in the presence of all three, if [the original owner or creditor] went back and forgave it, it is not forgiven. And this is explained in several places.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 144a:9:2.english: "He left grown sons" until "in the presence of the three of them he acquired" - Up to here is the position of Rabbi A. (HaRa"a), of blessed memory:
